protocol: D-000 turn 2 of 3, same cycle as turn 1; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN scoped D-006 fleet-class successor plus RULE-GOVERNED naming of the v3 reserved G03/G04 identifiers
summary: Codex's ADV-D098-01 reverses a mechanism I praised at turn 1, and it is right for a reason stronger than the one I had in view: D-006 says the regress-only rule 'activates from the second qualified release onward', and turn 1's automatic rebaseline on any image roll would have suppressed a mandated rule by a route D-006 does not provide, since D-006's only escape is a full-form waiver with product and release authority, an expiry and a measured residual. Turn 2 makes image drift irrelevant instead of disqualifying by running the digest-pinned previous binary and the candidate on the same VM, so sameness holds within each pair and the twenty-one VMs may mix images as paired strata. The G04 series are now enumerated and their absolute bounds match D-006's four numbers exactly. Simulation gives eighteen named identifiers, one reserved cell which is G13, and zero survivals of PARTLY MET or 'fixed runner image'. Two notes.

selfCorrection.summary: At turn 1 I called the regression rule 'the better fix of the two' and praised both of its halves. One half undid the other, and the undoing suppressed a rule D-006 mandates.
selfCorrection.whatIDid: My turn-1 verdict said that 'running the previous and candidate binaries on the same VM in randomized order, and forcing a rebaseline whenever image identity or CPU brand moves, means the ten-percent rule measures the binary rather than the fleet.' I treated the pairing and the rebaseline trigger as complementary.
selfCorrection.whatIMissed: They are in tension. Once both binaries run on the same current VM, the image is identical for both by construction, so cross-release image drift cannot enter the comparison — which makes a rebaseline trigger keyed to image sameness unnecessary. Worse than unnecessary: because GitHub rolls its images weekly, that trigger would have fired routinely and dropped the comparison back to absolute numerals almost every release. D-006 is explicit that 'the FIRST qualified release qualifies against the clause 1–4 thresholds alone; the rule activates from the second qualified release onward', and it provides exactly one way out — waivers 'per the register's full form … product AND release authority, an expiry, a MEASURED RESIDUAL'. An automatic rebaseline is not that form. So turn 1 would have suspended an adopted rule by an invented mechanism, and I endorsed it.
selfCorrection.theDisciplineIFailedToApply: When an entry introduces a control and also a condition that suppresses the controlled comparison, ask first whether the control already handles what the condition guards against, and second whether the suppression route is one the governing decision authorises. I checked neither. I had even quoted D-006's falsifiability note in the same review — successor with the measurement attached, never a silent waiver — without applying it to the rebaseline clause sitting in front of me.
selfCorrection.pattern: This is the fourth finding in this family that I passed and Codex caught. Three of the four share a shape: I confirm a clause exists and is internally sensible, and do not test it against a neighbouring clause of the same entry or against the governing decision's own escape rules.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, preflight item 4: 'RAM: macos `sysctl -n hw.memsize` bytes; Linux `MemTotal` kB × 1024. GiB = bytes/1024³. Match 7/14/16 ±0.75 GiB'
notesNonBlocking.observation: Half of my turn-1 note is answered and half is not, and the disposition reads as though both were. The observable side is now fully specified — the exact command per platform, the kB-to-byte conversion for Linux, and the division by 1024³ — which is a real improvement over turn 1. What is unchanged is the thing the note was actually about: the figures 7, 14 and 16 still carry no unit. If they are GiB the ±0.75 window is comfortable slack for kernel reserve; if they are decimal GB the conversions are 6.52, 13.04 and 14.90 GiB, so the deviations are 0.48, 0.96 and 1.10 and only the 7 row can pass. The asymmetry remains the tell, since a window sized for kernel reserve does not scale with capacity while the GB-to-GiB gap does. I leave it a note for the same reasons as at turn 1 — preflight is fail-closed so a mis-sized window blocks sampling rather than corrupting a number, it surfaces on the first run, and the unit of a published external table is not something I can settle from this repository. One clause stating the unit, or expressing the bound as a percentage of the advertised figure, would close it.

The G03 series are defined for each state in {cold, warm} with p50, p95 and p99 computed for every series, and the paired formula then requires candidate_p / previous_p ≤ 1.10 'for each of those three'. D-006 does not bound warm p50. Its G03 clause reads 'cold-cache p50 ≤ 100 ms, p95 ≤ 150 ms, p99 ≤ 250 ms; warm p95 ≤ 50 ms, p99 ≤ 100 ms (all five percentiles bounded per turn-1 NOTE)' — three cold and two warm, and the parenthetical reads as a deliberate enumeration rather than an accident. So the regression rule as written reaches a quantity D-006 chose to leave unbounded. I considered raising this as a SHOULD-FIX by analogy with my own D-094 finding, where numerals that stayed constant meant something different once their binding class changed, and placed it lower for three reasons: this tightens rather than loosens, so no release passes that should have failed; no adopted numeral is altered; and whether warm p50 is a 'CORE quantity of clauses 1–4' within D-006's stated domain is genuinely arguable rather than plainly wrong. The entry is otherwise careful about domain — it says 'No pooling across commands or metrics' — so saying explicitly whether warm p50 is inside or outside the rule would finish that work.

The attack 'ADV-D098-01 not landed (weekly roll still disables 10%)' fails, and I checked the design rather than the wording. The rule now applies 'from the second qualified release' via paired current-VM execution: the digest-pinned previous binary P and candidate C run on the same accepted VM in randomized recorded order, so image identity and CPU brand are constant within each pair by construction. The entry states the consequence directly — 'Weekly image rolls do not suppress this rule. Sameness of image/brand is within each pair on that VM; the 21 VMs may mix weekly images as paired strata.' That is a stratified paired design, and it is why the turn-1 rebaseline trigger was not merely redundant but harmful.

The remaining rebaseline path is now reserved for a genuine impossibility and routed to D-006's own machinery: 'If P cannot execute on the current class, do not auto-rebaseline: open a reviewed successor or use D-006's full waiver.' That matches D-006's waiver form rather than inventing one.

The entry's 'activates from the second qualified release' matches.

The attack 'ADV-D098-02 not landed (sample/cache/RSS matrix still ambiguous)' fails. The per-VM sequence is now explicit for both cases: first release is purge, cold candidate, warm candidate immediately with no intervening command or binary, per command; second-or-later is purge, cold, warm for the first binary then purge, cold, warm for the second, with {P,C} order randomized and recorded. G04 is enumerated across three commands and two metrics, doctor read-only is one launch per sample with no warm pair, and the paired statistic is named per gate — percentiles for G03, median for G04.

The G04 absolute bounds are cited exactly. D-006 reads '`--help`/`--version` RSS: steady baseline ≤ 40 MB, peak ≤ 50 MB … `doctor` read-only RSS: steady baseline ≤ 60 MB, peak ≤ 100 MB', and the entry writes 'help/version 40/50 MB; doctor read-only 60/100 MB' with the same assignment. Requiring every accepted sample to meet the bound is stricter than a percentile and is stated as such.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The turn's substance is that Codex reversed a mechanism I had praised, and the reversal is correct on a ground I had not reached. My objection to turn 1, had I made it, would have been that the rebaseline trigger was redundant once the comparison was paired. The stronger point is that it was a suppression: weekly image rolls would have fired it routinely, D-006 mandates the rule from the second qualified release, and D-006's only exit is a full-form waiver with authority, expiry and a measured residual. Turn 2 removes the need for any exit by making image drift cancel inside each pair, and reserves rebaseline for the one case where the previous binary genuinely cannot run — routed to a reviewed successor or D-006's own waiver rather than to an invented mechanism. I have recorded that miss rather than absorbing it into the general account, because it is the fourth in this family and three of the four share one shape: I confirm a clause is internally sensible and do not test it against the clause beside it. My two notes are the RAM unit, half-answered and still resting on an external convention I cannot settle, and a new one — the paired rule as written reaches warm p50, which D-006 does not bound among its five percentiles. The second tightens rather than loosens, which is why it is a note and not a finding.
